items.title: Run a Python Script Automatically Every Day (cron + Windows Task Scheduler for Beginners)
items.description:
Make any Python script run by itself every day: cron on Mac and Linux, Task Scheduler on Windows. Step by step for complete beginners, including the mistake that breaks almost everyone's first schedule (and the two-line fix), how to read a cron schedule, and how to make sure a scheduled script never fails silently. Every output on screen is the real result of the code shown.

Chapters
0:00 The result
0:31 Why schedule a script?
0:47 The plan
1:03 The script
1:52 Mac and Linux: cron
2:08 How to read a cron schedule
2:26 Use full paths
2:46 Add the job: crontab -e
3:25 The mistake that breaks first schedules
3:43 The fix: use the script's own folder
4:16 Every day at 9 AM
4:42 Weekdays only
4:57 Cron cheat sheet
5:18 Mistake 2: minute and hour swapped
5:33 Windows: Task Scheduler
6:43 Mistake 3: the computer was asleep
7:02 Pro tips
7:39 Recap

todo.txt (practice file)
[x] Send invoice to Sunny Bakery
[ ] Update the price list
[ ] Back up the photos folder
[x] Reply to Dana
[ ] Order new printer paper

report.py (final version, safe to schedule)
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path

folder = Path(__file__).parent  # the folder this script lives in

tasks = (folder / "todo.txt").read_text().splitlines()
open_tasks = [t for t in tasks if t.startswith("[ ]")]

now = datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M")
line = f"{now}  {len(open_tasks)} open tasks\n"

with open(folder / "report.txt", "a") as f:
    f.write(line)
print(line, end="")

First version (works by hand, fails under cron: it looks for todo.txt in the wrong folder)
from datetime import datetime

tasks = open("todo.txt").read().splitlines()
open_tasks = [t for t in tasks if t.startswith("[ ]")]

now = datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M")
line = f"{now}  {len(open_tasks)} open tasks\n"

with open("report.txt", "a") as f:
    f.write(line)
print(line, end="")

The cron line (crontab -e), every day at 9:00
0 9 * * * /full/path/to/python3 /full/path/to/scripts/report.py >> /full/path/to/scripts/cron.log 2>&1
Find your own paths with:  which python3   and   pwd

Cron cheat sheet (minute  hour  day-of-month  month  day-of-week)
* * * * *  every minute (testing)  |  */15 * * * *  every 15 minutes  |  0 * * * *  every hour
0 9 * * *  every day at 9:00  |  30 8 * * 1-5  weekdays at 8:30  |  0 9 * * 1  Mondays at 9:00
0 0 1 * *  midnight on the 1st  |  0 9,17 * * *  9:00 and 17:00

Windows Task Scheduler
Command Prompt: where python  (copy the path ending in python.exe)
Task Scheduler, Create Basic Task, Trigger: Daily, Action: Start a program
Program/script: full path to python.exe  |  Add arguments: report.py  |  Start in: your scripts folder
Test: right-click the task, Run. Last Run Result 0x0 = success.

Common problems:
FileNotFoundError only when scheduled  -  use Path(__file__).parent (or fill in "Start in" on Windows)
Runs at 00:09 instead of 9:00  -  the first field is the minute, the second is the hour
Nothing happened and no error  -  add >> cron.log 2>&1 so output and errors are saved
Missed run  -  the computer was asleep; on Windows tick "Run task as soon as possible after a scheduled start is missed"
crontab -r deletes ALL your jobs  -  use crontab -e and delete one line instead
